question: Should maintainers wait for the contributor to rebase and prove this uneditable fork, or open a credited replacement branch for the canonical hook `accountId` bug?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible and the PR contains useful work, but the branch is conflicting, maintainers cannot modify it, and the missing live proof cannot be supplied by automated repair.

options.title: Ask Contributor To Refresh And Prove
options.body: The contributor rebases on current main, ports the hook fix to the current source-delivery and request-handler files, removes the changelog edit, updates docs, and adds redacted real multi-account delivery proof.

options.title: Open A Credited Replacement
options.body: A maintainer or repair lane rebuilds the narrow fix on current main while crediting this PR and the linked issue, but still requires real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Leave Blocked Until Evidence
options.body: Keep this PR and the linked issue open without repair until a clean branch and proof are available.

recommendation.title: Ask Contributor To Refresh And Prove
recommendation.body: The contributor rebases on current main, ports the hook fix to the current source-delivery and request-handler files, removes the changelog edit, updates docs, and adds redacted real multi-account delivery proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway hook ownership and current blame make `vincentkoc` the best routing candidate for deciding how to refresh the hook boundary.
